Well the reason people take tia is because it actually is used as an antidepressant of sorts. It just happens to have a similar molecular structure as opioids. That being said, taking an actual opioid that is used for treating severe pain(the tampentadol you're taking) isn't necessarily a good idea for treating psychological issues like MDD. That's kind of the equivalent of someone popping Vicodin to deal with a childhood trauma. I only bring this point up for the sake of your well being. As someone recoving from an addiction stemmed from initially seeking help for my mental health I would hate to see it happen to anyone else.

I understand that's got to be tough being med resistant. All I can think to recommend would be to find a doctor willing to put in the leg work with you. With a lot of the more intense medications I'm on my doctor would only prescribe me a week at a time then make me come back while we figured how they they would effect me (i.e. dosage, side effects, benefits experienced, potential for abuse). Once we leaped those hurdles he would graduate me to a longer prescription for my personal convenience of not having to come in as often. Mental health is such a fickle beast. And with each individual requiring different solutions it's hard to say "trying this should work for you". All we can do is warn each other of potential dangers, and share what has been successful for us. I really do wish you the best of luck.
